title: What each format can represent

marks.linked: held as an external community-standard file (not copied) and queried through the shared index
marks.convention: representable by convention: stored and read back through the public API in a general-purpose slot, structure lost or ad hoc

rules: the evidence decides; only a genuinely ambiguous cell gives the other tool the better mark, and its note starts with 'Judgement call'
AnnData (and SpatialData table) elements rated in their most favourable orientation
a test that needed a generic slot backs at most 'by convention', an external file 'linked'
a data table serialised to JSON text in a descriptive metadata attribute does not count (recorded with counted: false); provenance metadata there does

partial reads: native = one cell's / chromosome's rows are read from disk without reading the other rows (beyond the selection key column); by convention = only by scanning every row (streamed) or with part of the data loaded whole

hierarchy.note: spots → traces → cells via trace_id / cell_id; traces and cells tables

cell_pos.note: set_cell_spatial_coordinates() writes two extra columns of the cells table (spatial_x / spatial_y, names configurable) and a uns['cell_spatial'] record (coordinate system, source); 2-D only, no outline, and not a schema element of spec.md (which only suggests x_centroid-style cells columns)

test.detail: set_cell_spatial_coordinates: two extra columns of the cells table (spatial_x, spatial_y) + a uns['cell_spatial'] record; 2-D, no outline

contacts.note: linked, not copied: uns['linked_scool' / 'linked_cool'] records path, bin size and cell map; load_linked_scool / Dataset.contacts(group=) read them (test: a real .scool read back after the round trip). Our own call: the pixels stay in the external .scool / .cool by design.

test.detail: link_scool → uns['linked_scool'] record; load_linked_scool(cell='c1') reads the external .scool after the round trip

intervals.note: intervals: typed IntervalTable (domain / pair / peak / segment); TADs as domain, loops as pair

points.note: points: non-genomic 3-D points in the coords frame

provenance.note: results: ResultsStore of ResultRecord(kind, params, function, version, inputs, created_utc)

partial.note: read(backed=True): get_cell / get_trace / get_chrom read only the needed row ranges (index/ runs; Fig. 2d)

hierarchy.note: Spot_ID → Trace_ID → Cell_ID in the core table; Trace Data and Cell Data tables indexed by Trace_ID / Cell_ID

spot_signals.note: Spot Biological Data / Spot Quality tables indexed by Spot_ID (user-defined columns declared with #^ lines)

bin_signals.note: none of the 12 tables is indexed by genomic locus; a per-locus value can only be repeated on every spot as an optional column

cells.note: Cell Data table (4dn_FOF-CT_cell), mandatorily indexed by Cell_ID, with optional user-defined columns (cell type, volume, ...)

cell_emb.note: no embedding slot: the Cell Data table's columns are scalar optional columns, so an embedding is one #^ column per dimension

audit.reason: split from 'cells & embeddings': FOF-CT has a cell table but no multi-dimensional per-cell slot

cell_pos.note: Cell/ROI Mapping table (4dn_FOF-CT_mapping; conditionally required whenever a Cell Data table is deposited): ROI_Boundaries of each Cell_ID in global coordinates, format declared in ##ROI_Boundaries_Format (OME polygon or OBJ mesh) + ##XYZ_Unit. Outline native; a centroid only as an optional column

contacts.note: no contact-matrix table in the 12 FOF-CT tables

intervals.note: no genomic-interval table (the Sub-Cell ROI table's 'Chromosome_Domain' is a spatial ROI, not a genomic interval); domain labels only as an optional per-spot column, loops (pairs) not representable

points.note: RNA Spot Data table (RNA_Spot_ID, X, Y, Z, Gene_ID, RNA_name, link ids)

provenance.note: header #Software_* fields describe the tools that produced a table; analysis results only as optional columns

partial.note: plain CSV without an index: one cell or chromosome is found only by scanning every row (streamed, e.g. pandas chunksize, so memory stays bounded)

coords.note: obsm['spatial'] (n_obs, 3), a community convention; no trace / unit structure

hierarchy.note: one obs axis: cell_id / trace_id only as obs columns; spots and cells cannot both be observations

spot_signals.note: spots as obs: X / layers / obs columns

bin_signals.note: loci as var (cells × loci, as for scATAC peaks): var table. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

cells.note: cells as obs: obs table. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

cell_emb.note: cells as obs: obsm (X_umap, X_pca), the slot designed for per-observation multi-dimensional annotations. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

cell_pos.note: cells as obs: obsm['spatial'] (n_cells, 2), the squidpy / scanpy convention; not an AnnData schema element (no coordinate system, unit or outline)

test.detail: cells as obs, obsm['spatial'] (squidpy convention; no coordinate system, no outline)

contacts.note: no contact-map type: one dense or sparse locus × locus matrix can be put in varp (loci as var), without pixel/balancing schema, resolutions or per-cell maps. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

test.detail: one locus × locus matrix in varp

points.note: a DataFrame in uns (or a second AnnData)

provenance.note: free-form dicts in uns (scanpy writes uns['<tool>']['params'])

partial.note: Judgement call: anndata.experimental.read_lazy (0.12, experimental API) opens obs as a lazy xarray Dataset and obsm / X as dask arrays; a cell mask reads the cell_id column, to_memory() then reads only the selected chunks. No per-cell index.

test.detail: read_lazy: obs / obsm / X are lazy (xarray / dask); mask from the cell_id column, to_memory() reads only the selected chunks

coords.note: points element with x, y, z (3-D points are supported) and coordinate-system transformations

hierarchy.note: cell_id / trace_id as columns of the points; a table annotates one element level (region + instance_key), no nested cell › trace › spot

spot_signals.note: a table annotating the spots points element (region + instance_key = spot_id); test uses this, not extra point columns

test.detail: a table annotating the spots points (region='spots', instance_key='spot_id')

bin_signals.note: Judgement call: no genomic locus axis among the spatial elements, but a table is an AnnData: loci as var of a cells × loci table annotating the cell shapes, var columns = per-locus signals, as for AnnData (test uses this orientation instead of a dummy table annotating no element). Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

test.detail: var column of a cells × loci table annotating the cell shapes

cells.note: shapes (or labels) for cells + a table annotating them

cell_emb.note: obsm of the table annotating the cells

cell_pos.note: shapes element: circles (centroid + radius) or polygons (outline), with coordinate-system transformations

test.detail: shapes elements: circles (centroid + radius) and polygons (outline), each with a coordinate-system transformation

contacts.note: no contact-map element: a table is an AnnData, so one locus × locus matrix in varp, as for AnnData

test.detail: one locus × locus matrix in varp of a table

intervals.note: interval rows as obs of a table annotating no element

test.detail: interval rows as obs of a table annotating no element

partial.note: points are lazy dask DataFrames without an index on cell or chromosome: a filter on cell_id then compute() streams every partition (Fig. 2d, 0.75 s at 1e7 spots). Spatial bounding-box / polygon queries are native but select by space, not by cell or chromosome.

audit.reason: criterion made explicit: a full partition scan is 'by convention'

test.detail: lazy dask points: a filter on cell_id streams every partition (no index)

hierarchy.note: spots and cells as separate modalities; the link is an obs column, no parent / child relation

test.detail: trace_id / cell_id obs columns of the spots modality

bin_signals.note: var of a cells × loci modality

test.detail: var of a cells × loci modality

cells.note: global obs or the obs of a cells modality

cell_emb.note: obsm of a cells modality, or the global obsm (multimodal embeddings)

cell_pos.note: obsm['spatial'] of a cells modality (the AnnData / squidpy convention)

contacts.note: no contact-map type: varp of a cells × loci modality (one matrix, as for AnnData)

test.detail: one locus × locus matrix in varp
an RNA-spot modality, positions in obsm['spatial']
